skill.name: c-pro

content.value_statement: C projects often fail through unclear ownership, unchecked errors, and weak validation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward safer C99/C11 implementations.
actual_capabilities: Plans C99 and C11 implementations with explicit memory ownership.
Reviews pointer usage, allocation paths, and cleanup responsibilities.
Suggests POSIX system call handling and return value checks.
Outlines Makefile flags, header guards, and unit test coverage.
Recommends debugging and profiling steps with gdb, Valgrind, and benchmarks.
limitations: It does not execute compiled programs or verify runtime behavior by itself.
It cannot guarantee portability across every compiler, libc, or embedded target.
It depends on complete requirements, platform details, and build constraints.
It is not a substitute for project-specific security review.

use_cases.title: Design a C Module
use_cases.description: Plan APIs, ownership rules, headers, and error paths before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Memory Safety
use_cases.description: Check allocation, pointer, and cleanup paths for leaks and invalid access.

use_cases.title: Prepare Embedded Code
use_cases.description: Reduce stack use, clarify resource limits, and add focused validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Safe C Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write a C99 function for [task]. Include ownership rules, error handling, and expected inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Review Pointer and Memory Use
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this C code for pointer errors, leaks, double frees, and missing return value checks: [paste code].

prompt_templates.title: Design a POSIX Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a POSIX C component for [goal]. Include API shape, system calls, failure handling, tests, and build flags.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize After Profiling
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these profiling results for my C program: [paste findings]. Propose changes that preserve correctness and ownership clarity.

output_examples.input: A request to build a buffered file reader in C.
output_examples.output: A design with ownership rules, POSIX read handling, cleanup paths, Makefile flags, and tests for short reads and failures.

output_examples.input: A pointer-heavy parser with suspected leaks.
output_examples.output: A review that identifies allocation lifetimes, missing frees, unchecked returns, and a Valgrind verification plan.
A profiling-first plan covering lock contention, queue structure, benchmark cases, and correctness checks.

best_practices: Define memory ownership before writing or changing C code.
Check every allocation, system call, and library return value.
Validate changes with compiler warnings, tests, Valgrind, and targeted benchmarks.
anti_patterns: Optimizing code before measuring the real bottleneck.
Returning raw pointers without clear lifetime and cleanup rules.
Ignoring platform constraints when writing POSIX or embedded code.

faq.question: What kind of C work does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports systems programming, memory management, POSIX APIs, pthreads, embedded constraints, debugging, testing, and performance review.

faq.question: Can it write complete C files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft C source, headers, Makefile guidance, tests, and validation steps when requirements are clear.

faq.question: Does it run Valgrind or gdb?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend commands and interpret results, but execution depends on the host environment.

faq.question: Which C standards does it target?
faq.answer: The skill text targets C99 and C11, with attention to POSIX behavior when relevant.

faq.question: Is it useful for embedded development?
faq.answer: Yes. It can address stack use, resource limits, allocation strategy, and validation for constrained targets.

faq.question: How should I get the best results?
faq.answer: Provide compiler, platform, constraints, sample code, expected behavior, and any test or profiler output.
